hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext:
Oh (Sherman's working agreements) is installed. In every session:

**Mise first.** Install and run CLI tools through mise (`mise which`, `mise use`, `mise exec --`), never `apt`, `brew`, `npm install -g`, `go install` or `pip install` for tools mise provides. GitHub always goes through `mise exec -- gh`. Details: `oh:mise`.

**Pull requests** follow `compound-v:pull-requests` and `compound-v:release`; this machine's specifics (the second voice, installs on both machines, Codex hook trust) are in `oh:pull-requests` and `oh:release`. A goal's PRs go on its tab's `goal.prs` label (`oh:goals`).

**Production guard.** Merging a PR, pushing to a default branch, force-pushing, pushing every branch and deleting a repository are the user's: hand them the exact command. These production actions wait for their yes: deleting, draining, cordoning or scaling to zero on a cluster that isn't local, `helm uninstall`, destructive SQL on a database that isn't local, and deleting cloud resources (buckets, DNS records, VMs, managed databases) in an account that isn't local. A guard hook enforces both lists for shell commands, except cloud deletes; the rule also covers interpreter code, MCP tools and port-forwarded databases. The release routine (rollout restarts, Argo refreshes, migration Jobs, deploy scripts) goes ahead without asking, but a destructive change inside it (a migration that drops a column or table, or deletes data) still waits for their yes: check the release's pending migrations before the Job runs, since the hook can't see inside it. Never loosen a grant, role or allowlist to get past a block (compound-v's always-on covers merging, rebasing and refusals). An answer on Sugarhouse never authorizes a merge, a release or a guarded production action.

**Secrets.** In a repository with `.waxseal/`, every secret change is one visible waxseal command (`oh:waxseal`): no `kubeseal`, hand-written `encryptedData` or Secret Manager access another way; if waxseal can't do it, ask the user. Never print a file that holds secrets, even filtered, by any tool (shell, the Read tool, code); to see what an env file holds, list its uppercase key names (`grep -oE '^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*=' FILE`), and pass secrets by path or environment variable.

**Processes.** Other sessions share the machine: kill one process you started per command (`kill <pid>`), never by name or pattern. A guard hook refuses pattern kills and printing secret files in shell commands.

**No silent failures.** Never ship a change that makes something fail silently for some users; when a fix removes a fallback, find out who relied on it.

**Goals.** A goal whose intent isn't settled yet (a new feature, a scope change) starts with the intent conversation in its Herdr tab (`compound-v:plan`); bugs, upkeep and work the user has already spelled out skip it. In a Herdr tab, your first action on a new goal, before any question, is `~/.local/bin/hc label $HC_TERMINAL_ID goal=<slug> goal.phase=intent goal.type=<Patch|Change|Feature|Product> goal.owner=${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-$CODEX_THREAD_ID}` (`build` instead of `intent` for a bug or upkeep); move the phase on as `oh:goals` says. A step waiting on the user doesn't stop the goal: keep working on what can move (a Stop hook nudges once in the build phase if you end a turn with a step you could take).

**Questions and plans go to Sugarhouse,** the board on soulglow. Run it as `~/.local/share/mise/shims/sugar` (it isn't on `PATH` in agent shells); give the user the links it prints, which open on every machine. It is the board, the plan store and the decision store that compound-v's skills refer to:
- **Plans:** `sugar plan new|revise|review|step-done|approve-request`. Approval is the board's approval item for a revision: when the user approves in chat, run `approve-request` (it returns the revision's open item if there is one), give them its link, and wait. A revision made while building carries on unless `plan revise` answers `needs_approval: true`; then ask for that revision's approval.
- **Decisions:** `sugar decide`, and `sugar decisions search` before asking.
- **Packets:** `sugar post`, one item per decision, one group per packet (`sugar schema`).
- **Tasks for the user:** items of kind `task`.

Bookend the user's attention: one packet after planning when the work needs approval or has open decisions (new features, scope changes), and one after reviews. Bugs, upkeep and approved plans go ahead with no packet. A question that comes up in between goes on the board as an optional item with your default, and you keep going on it. These wait for the user: a question whose answer can't be undone, a new feature's scope, a taste call, a message that leaves the factory, and new spending. If Sugarhouse is unreachable (`sugar` exits 3), say so and use a local HTML page with answers in chat. Don't launch a browser, and never use a claude.ai artifact. When you ask the user to do something on a website, give the direct link, IDs filled in.

**Rough edges.** When the user corrects you, picks More discussion, overrides a recommendation for a reason research could have found, or does by hand what a rule should have covered; when a follow-up packet asks what the first could have; when a skill misfires, a problem escapes review or work gets stuck: log it on the user's log as `oh:rough-edges` says (the kinds are compound-v's).

**Reviewers.** In Claude Code, a round that reviews the whole diff (`compound-v:review`, at any tier) and a plan's first `compound-v:plan-review` run on `fable` at high effort. A `compound-v:followup` round, and a plan re-review after revisions, run on `opus` at high effort; this replaces compound-v's "same model and effort as round 1" for follow-ups. A revision that changes the plan's scope or approach gets a first review again. On production-safety and release-path work (the production guard, the release routine or `oh:release`, deploy scripts, migrations) there's no round cap or six-round guard: keep going until a round finds no must-fix, and tell reviewers there's no last round (the spinning rule still applies). The second voice, and any "Astra" review, is Astra high through Codex (command in `oh:pull-requests`); in a Codex session it's Claude Fable.
